01.missing: Only a ruling about a mortar in Mar Shmuel's house and its reason; nothing turns.

02.event: Rabbi Tarfon bent down so his mother could step on him to get into and out of bed, and boasted of it in the study hall.
02.turn: The sages told him he had not reached even half the honor due her.
02.outcome: They asked whether she had ever thrown his purse into the sea in front of him without his shaming her, deflating his boast.
02.summary: Rabbi Tarfon honored his mother by letting her climb onto his back to get into and out of bed. He came and praised himself for this in the study hall. The sages answered that he had not reached even half of the honor owed to her: had she ever thrown his purse into the sea before his eyes without his embarrassing her?

03.actor: a woman whose husband had died, and the people at Rabbi Yehuda's court
03.event: A woman came to Rabbi Yehuda's court and the people there told her to lament her husband, tear her clothes and loosen her hair.
03.turn: They coached her to show grief so that Rabbi Yehuda, who requires it, would believe her.
03.summary: A woman came to Rabbi Yehuda's court to testify that her husband had died. The people there told her to lament him, tear her clothes and let down her hair, so that Rabbi Yehuda would accept her and allow her to remarry. The Gemara explains they were not teaching her to lie, since they held she could remarry anyway.
03.missing: Whether Rabbi Yehuda permitted her to remarry.

04.missing: A legal dispute citing, as evidence, that many were re-circumcised in Bar Kokhba's days; no individual event is told.

05.actor: Rabbi Abbahu (or Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba), Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi
05.event: Rabbi Abbahu sat and reported in Rabbi Yohanan's name that the halakha follows Rabbi Yohanan ben Beroka.
05.turn: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi turned their faces away in silent disagreement.
05.outcome: They said nothing aloud, out of respect for Rabbi Abbahu's standing at Caesar's court.
05.summary: Rabbi Abbahu sat and taught in Rabbi Yohanan's name that the halakha follows Rabbi Yohanan ben Beroka. Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi, sitting opposite him, turned their faces away to show they disagreed with the report. Some say the speaker was Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba; Rav Pappa notes that only Rabbi Abbahu's ties to Caesar's court explain why they kept silent.
05.missing: The incident is told as evidence and the speaker's identity is disputed; little resolution beyond the gesture.

06.actor: a man who betrothed a woman conditionally, and the Sages
06.event: A man betrothed a woman on a condition that was not fulfilled and then had relations with her.
06.turn: The Sages could not declare the betrothal void.
06.outcome: They could not release her without a bill of divorce.
06.summary: Rav Kahana, citing Ulla, reports an actual case: a man betrothed a woman conditionally, the condition failed, and he later lived with her. The Sages found they had no power to let her go without a bill of divorce, so a divorce was required.
06.missing: The incident is reported only in outline; names and details are absent.

07.actor: a maidservant of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's household
07.event: The maidservant immersed herself in a ritual bath and came out.
07.turn: A bone was found between her teeth.
07.outcome: Rabbi required her to immerse again.
07.summary: A maidservant in Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's household immersed for purity and came up out of the water. Then a bone was found stuck between her teeth. Rabbi ruled that the immersion did not count and made her immerse a second time.

08.actor: Rav Yosef and his student Abaye
08.event: Rav Yosef said he had never heard a certain halakha.
08.turn: Abaye reminded him that Rav Yosef himself had taught it to them, along with the source and three lessons drawn from it.
08.summary: When a teaching was cited, Rav Yosef said he had never heard it. His student Abaye told him he had taught it to them himself, on Rav Huna's ruling about a side post along an alleyway wall, and recited the three conclusions Rav Yosef had drawn from it. The English note explains Rav Yosef had forgotten his learning through illness.
08.missing: Rav Yosef's reaction; the illness is supplied only by the translator's note.

09.event: A woman's husband went overseas and she gave birth twelve months after he left.
09.turn: Rava Tosfa'a ruled the child legitimate, presuming a delayed pregnancy.
09.outcome: The child was declared fit (not a mamzer).
09.summary: A woman's husband went abroad, and twelve months after he left she gave birth. Rava Tosfa'a ruled that the child was the husband's and legitimate, on the view that a pregnancy can be delayed. The Gemara then asks whose opinion that ruling followed.
09.missing: The case is cited as a legal precedent; the people's reactions are absent.

10.actor: a man whose betrothed died; Rav Nahman, Ulla, Avimei and Rav Hiyya bar Ami
10.event: A man whose betrothed had died came before the sages, who told him to bury her or pay her marriage contract.
10.turn: Rav Hiyya objected with a mishna that a betrothed man does not inherit his betrothed.
10.summary: Rav Nahman, Ulla and Avimei bar Rav Pappi were sitting with Rav Hiyya bar Ami when a man came whose betrothed had died. They told him to bury her or pay her heirs her marriage contract. Rav Hiyya objected, citing a teaching that a betrothed husband does not inherit from her.

11.actor: Rav Yehuda, his father Rav Yehezkel, and Shmuel
11.event: Rav Yehuda corrected the way his father Rav Yehezkel taught a mishna, and argued the point with him.
11.turn: Shmuel rebuked Rav Yehuda for speaking to his father that way.
11.outcome: Shmuel taught him the proper, indirect way to correct a parent.
11.summary: Rav Yehezkel was teaching his son Rami a mishna about condemned criminals who became mixed up. His other son, Rav Yehuda, said: Father, do not teach it that way, and argued for his own version, answering his father's objection too. Later Shmuel told Rav Yehuda not to speak to his father like that, and taught that one should correct a parent only by quoting the verse, so the parent understands on his own.

12.missing: A fragment of an exegetical argument about the Israelites eating after the omer; no narrated event.

13.event: Rav Hisda praised Rav Hamnuna to Rav Huna, who asked to meet him.
13.turn: Rav Huna saw Rav Hamnuna had no head-cloth and learned he was unmarried.
13.outcome: Rav Huna turned his face away and told him not to see his face until he married.
13.summary: Rav Hisda kept praising Rav Hamnuna to Rav Huna as a great man, so Rav Huna asked to have him sent over. When Rav Hamnuna came, Rav Huna noticed he did not wear a scholar's head-cloth, and Rav Hamnuna explained he was not married. Rav Huna turned his face away and told him not to come into his presence again until he married.

14.actor: the sons of Rav Huna bar Avin
14.event: They bought a maidservant for coins they did not have, leaving a piece of silver as collateral.
14.turn: The maidservant's price rose and the sellers wanted to back out.
14.outcome: Rabbi Ami ruled there had been no valid purchase.
14.summary: The sons of Rav Huna bar Avin agreed to buy a maidservant for copper coins, but lacking the money they left a piece of silver as security. Later her value rose and the sellers wanted to cancel. They came before Rabbi Ami, who ruled that neither coins nor silver had been paid, so no sale had taken place.

15.missing: A question put to Rabbi Eliezer and his answer, used to infer a legal view; no event.

16.event: In Mar Shmuel's days there was some lentil bread, which he threw to his dog.
16.turn: Even the dog would not eat it.
16.summary: Some lentil bread was made in Mar Shmuel's time. He threw it to his dog, and even the dog refused to eat it. The Gemara cites this to question whether lentil bread is food.
16.missing: Cited only as an objection; little beyond the single episode.

17.event: A woman meant to invite her neighbor to come and eat milk.
17.turn: Because of her slurred pronunciation she instead said, May a lioness eat you.
17.summary: A Galilean woman wanted to say to her neighbor, Come, I will give you milk to eat. Because Galileans swallowed their guttural letters, what came out was, May a lioness eat you.
17.missing: The neighbor's reaction; it is an illustrative anecdote.

18.missing: Describes Mareimar's practice of closing Sura's alleyways with nets and his reason; no event that turns.

19.event: Bar Shatya, who was sometimes insane, sold property.
19.turn: Two witnesses said he sold it while sane and two others said while insane.
19.outcome: Rav Ashi let the testimonies cancel and left the land in Bar Shatya's possession.
19.summary: Bar Shatya, a man who had bouts of insanity, sold some land. One pair of witnesses testified that he was sane at the time, and another pair that he was insane. Rav Ashi ruled that the two pairs cancel each other out, so the land stays in Bar Shatya's possession.

20.event: Seven teachings were said on Shabbat morning before Rav Hisda in Sura.
20.turn: The same teachings were repeated that afternoon before Rava in Pumbedita, too far to have walked on Shabbat.
20.summary: Seven teachings were stated one Shabbat morning before Rav Hisda in Sura. By the end of that same Shabbat they were repeated before Rava in Pumbedita, though the two cities were too far apart for anyone to travel between them on Shabbat. The Gemara goes on to ask who could have brought them.
20.missing: Who carried the teachings; the context only speculates (Elijah or Yosef the demon).
